page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The CPU includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in single-core and multi-core processing, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2074.0 and a multi-core score of 15951.0. The processor demonstrates high efficiency in cryptographic and compression tasks, achieving 33.6 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 35678.6 in the PassMark CPU encryption test. Memory performance is characterized by a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 2625.73 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write bandwidths reach 162.39 GB/sec and 83.85 GB/sec, respectively. In web serving benchmarks, the instance delivers a static web serving throughput of 51.12 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7i-flex family offers a resource-dense compute profile without the higher cost of local NVMe storage, making it a viable option for workloads that rely on network-attached storage. However, the lack of local storage and dedicated GPUs limits its utility for heavy local database caching or large-scale GPU-accelerated deep learning. The instance is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as web serving, software compilation, text and image processing, and moderate machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its text generation speed of 286.26 tokens/second on small LLM models.
